analysis.title: FX Risk Index: Point of inflection?
key_insights: CACIB FX Risk Index at -0.8904 (vs -0.8691 last week), a little further into risk-seeking territory but just above its flat 100-day moving average. The coming week could decide between a decisive shift toward risk reduction or a return to risk-seeking.
The Index has retreated toward its trend in recent weeks. The report says such a crossover often signals a more prolonged retreat in risk.
AI equities sold off on disappointment with the Q3 earnings season and concern about the AI investment boom under a Democrat-controlled US Congress.

Sentiment has been supported by a potential end to the US-Iran conflict and lower oil prices. The US appears to see its blockade of Iranian oil exports as enough economic pressure to force a deal without military force.
Investors bought the dip in AI stocks despite a jump in UST yields this week, which raises the discount rate on those equities' future earnings.
Challenge to the sentiment bounce: Iran says it will not allow any enriched uranium out of the country, a key US requirement for a deal.

Nvidia is a swing factor. There are reports its board wants to replace CEO Jensen Huang, who is at the centre of Nvidia's circular financing of AI infrastructure investors (chip deals, equity investments, revenue guarantees, debt support).
Index drivers over the past week: higher equity and FX volatility and defensive stocks outperforming cyclicals supported the Index. Lower gold prices and private-credit spreads dragged it lower.
Among G10 currencies, only CHF, CAD and SEK have significant positive correlations with the Risk Index. GBP, USD and NOK have significant negative correlations.
